neighbours.label: ' just' as a limiter in a negated or dismissive frame (X just isn't, you can't just, just because); not temporal 'just' (had just arrived) or 'just' meaning fair
fire: The old bridge just isn't strong enough for heavy trucks.
Cheap paint just doesn't last through a wet winter.
These tiny batteries just aren't powerful enough for a drill.
The rules are strict here; you can't just park wherever you like.
A good essay takes work, and you can't just copy the first thing you find.
The landlord can't just raise the rent without a notice.
Nobody should be ignored just because they speak quietly.
The plan was dropped just because one manager disliked it.
quiet: The old bridge was just repaired after the heavy floods.
Cheap paint only lasts through one wet winter.
These tiny batteries have just arrived from the factory.
The rules are strict here, and the judge is known as a fair and just man.
A good essay takes work, and I have just finished the first draft.
The landlord simply raised the rent without a notice.
Nobody noticed that the train had just left the station.
The plan was dropped merely to please one manager.

notes: The other side: the - pole fires where a limiter is about to come ('rather than [just]', 'for informational purposes [only]') and this pole's output suppresses ' only' / ' just' / ' merely'. The top examples also hold Japanese だけ / ただ (a probe read 0.29), not tested here. Probe readings were modest (0.15-0.42).
